title: Karhunen-Lo\`{e}ve Expansion of Time-Rescaled Brownian Bridge and Inference of Unit Distribution
authors: Leonardo Chhabra, Anindya Goswami, Nikhil Thekkedath Haridas
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33166v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the Karhunen-Lo\`{e}ve (KL) basis of the time-rescaled Brownian bridge (TRBB) with time rescales of the form $t\mapsto\int_0^t f^2(s)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}s$. For testing unit distributions, we construct a new statistic based on the projection of empirical process onto the KL basis functions of the TRBB and derive its asymptotic distribution. Moreover, using this statistic, we develop a goodness-of-fit test for uniformity and study its power against a specific non-uniform alternative. Numerical experiments indicate that, in the settings considered, the proposed test can have higher power than classical alternatives such as the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Cram\'{e}r-von Mises tests. Furthermore, we propose a two-parameter family of TRBBs and derive the closed-form KL expansion for this new deterministically time-changed process. The family includes a diverse class of monotone rate time rescales, both increasing and decreasing, while retaining a tractable eigenstructure. Finally, an analysis with real data reveals greater flexibility of the proposed parametric family for modelling monotone densities on $[0,1]$.

title: On a Problem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham Related to Restricted Order
authors: Shi-Qiang Chen, Quan-Hui Yang, Lilu Zhao
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33191v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $A$ be a set of nonnegative integers. We prove that if $A\setminus F$ has a finite order for every finite subset $F\subseteq A$, then $A$ has finite restricted order. This resolves a problem posed by Erd\H{o}s and Graham in 1980. We also establish a local to global principle to characterize restricted asymptotic bases of finite order.

title: A $q$-analogue of an inverse problem leading to second-order linear functionals
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33207v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: R. Sfaxi studied the linear functional $L_\epsilon$ determined by the equation $L_\epsilon-\epsilon L_\epsilon'=L$. We replace the derivative by the Hahn operator $H_q$ and study the solution $L_\epsilon$ of $L_\epsilon-\epsilon H_q L_\epsilon=L$. For $0<q><1$ we solve the equation explicitly when $L$ is a Dirac mass, and we deduce that $L_\epsilon$ is positive-definite whenever $\epsilon>0$ and $L$ is positive-definite on $[0,+\infty)$. We show that $L_\epsilon$ is $H_q$-semiclassical if and only if $EL=FL_\epsilon$ for two non-zero polynomials $E$ and $F$, and we work out the $q$-analogues of the Hermite and Laguerre examples. Finally we treat the $H_q$-classical functional $K_q$ whose moments are the $q$-factorials: here $L_\epsilon=(1+\epsilon)^{-1}(K_q+\epsilon\,h_{-\epsilon}K_q)$, and for $\epsilon<0$ the functional $L_\epsilon$ is positive-definite if and only if

title: Besicovitch Pseudo Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes and Their Applications to Delayed Stochastic Neural Networks
authors: Yongkun Li, Yuwei Cao, Bing Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33209v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Besicovitch almost periodic concept is a generalization of the Bohr, Stepanov, and Weyl almost periodic concepts and, in a certain sense, has broader coverage and weaker conditions. However, the concept of pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes in the Besicovitch sense has not yet been systematically proposed, which limits the characterization of the complex oscillatory behavior of a broader class of stochastic non-autonomous systems. This paper proposes the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes. As an application of this concept, we study the existence of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic solutions in distribution for a class of stochastic delayed neural networks in which all parameters except the time delays are pseudo almost periodic and establish stability criteria for such solutions in the $p$-th mean sense. The work of this paper fills the gap caused by the lack of the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes and provides a new conceptual tool and analytical approach for characterizing the complex oscillatory behavior of stochastic differential equations and stochastic neural network systems.

title: Crossed homomorphisms on Leibniz superalgebras
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33211v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this article, we give characterisation of crossed homomorphisms of Leibniz superalgebras as Maurer-Cartan elements of an associated graded Lie algebra. This characterization enables us to develop a cohomology theory for crossed homomorphisms and to apply it to their formal deformation theory. We show that the infinitesimal of a deformation is a 1-cocycle and that linear deformations are classified by such cocycles. Furthermore, we introduce the category of crossed homomorphisms between two fixed Leibniz superalgebras.

title: Why $(4x(1-x))^{3/4}$ approximates the binary entropy so well: a proof of Tops{\o}e's convexity conjecture
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33213v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Write the binary entropy as $h(x) = u^{g(x)}$ with $u = 4x(1-x)$. Topsoe (2001) proved the sharp bounds $1/\ln 4 \le g \le 1$, i.e. $u \le h \le u^{1/\ln 4}$, and conjectured that the effective exponent $g$ is convex. We prove this conjecture. In the variable $s = (1-2x)^2$, $g$ extends to a Pick function on $\mathbb{C} \setminus [1,\infty)$ with an explicit positive density on the cut, so that $g(x) = \sum_n \gamma_n (1-2x)^{2n}$ with $\gamma_n > 0$ and $(\gamma_n)_{n \ge 1}$ a moment sequence. Pinelis's monotonicity theorem, Topsoe's power-type bounds and the optimality of their exponents follow as corollaries, together with a classification of all exponents $\alpha$ for which $u^\alpha$ bounds $h$. The proof is by hand except for one inequality in one real variable on a bounded interval, certified by interval arithmetic. As an application we give sharp, certified constants for the approximation $h \approx u^{3/4}$: $-0.0065493 \le u^{3/4} - h \le 0.0080004$ on $[0,1]$.

title: Why $2$, $3$, and $5$? Lambert Series, Prime Logarithms, and a $48$-Step Octave for Musical Tuning
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33219v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The primes $2$, $3$, and $5$ generate many familiar frequency ratios in musical tuning. We identify three mathematical properties that distinguish these primes in a construction based on modular transformations of Lambert series. We derive an exact identity for $\log p$ for every odd prime $p$, together with a separate identity for $\log2$. Within this construction, all transformed Lambert-series arguments can be chosen real precisely for $p=2,3,5$. In the identities obtained for these three primes, every series argument has magnitude at most $e^{-2\pi}$, whereas the identity for $\log7$ requires complex arguments and contains a more slowly converging series.
  The leading $\pi$-terms for $\log2$, $\log3$, and $\log5$ generate a $48$-step octave grid and recover its conventional prime mapping $(48,76,111)$ exactly, without rounding, while including the leading $\pi$-term for $\log7$ enlarges the grid to $1680$ steps. The identity for $\log7$ introduces no auxiliary logarithms of larger primes, whereas for every prime $11\le p<20000$, an exact computation identifies such logarithms in the construction.
  The Lambert-series remainders provide exact corrections for just intervals and musical commas. For a published theoretical model of $22$ Hindustani shrutis, the additive $48$-step mapping assigns all $22$ ratios to distinct positions, with corrections no greater than $15.3$ cents in magnitude. These results establish precise arithmetic distinctions that parallel the prominence of $5$-limit tuning, without implying that number theory determines musical practice.

title: hp-Adaptive Finite Element Modeling of Static Cracks in Density-Dependent Media
authors: Vicente Valle Martinez, Saugata Ghosh, S. M. Mallikarjunaiah, Dambaru Bhatta
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33220v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The elastostatic crack-tip fields within a density-dependent continuum are numerically investigated under several macroscopic loading configurations. The governing nonlinear boundary value problem is formulated using an algebraically nonlinear hyperelastic constitutive relationship in which the material moduli are intrinsically coupled to volumetric strain. Existence and uniqueness of the weak solution to the nonlinear displacement-based variational formulation are rigorously established at the continuous level via the Minty-Browder theorem. The variational formulation is then linearized at the partial differential equation level to construct a continuous damped Newton-Raphson scheme. To accurately capture the severe field gradients and internal singularities inherent to this model, the resulting sequence of linear operator equations is discretized and solved via a conforming finite element method within an $hp$-adaptive framework. A comparative analysis is conducted across five distinct boundary loading profiles (encompassing uniform, piecewise-slope, and concentrated point loads) applied to a stationary cracked geometry. Within each configuration, the density-dependent constitutive parameter is systematically varied to assess its regulatory impact on the fracture process zone, focusing on the spatial evolution of normal stress, normal strain, and strain energy density near the crack tip. Numerical results demonstrate that local kinematic deformability is strictly bounded by the strain-limiting nature of the continuum, whereby static equilibrium is sustained through severe, localized stress amplifications. Furthermore, the mechanical influence of the modeling parameter is fundamentally dictated by the topological interplay between internal crack geometry and the spatial distribution of applied macroscopic loads.

title: Cyclicity of period annuli of quadratic codimension four centers
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33230v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quadratic systems with a center fall into four classes: Hamiltonian $Q_3^H$, reversible $Q_3^R$, generalized Lotka--Volterra $Q_3^{LV}$, and codimension-four $Q_4$. Before this work, the cyclicity of period annuli under quadratic perturbations had been completely determined for $Q_3^H$, whereas only certain special cases had been resolved for $Q_3^R$, $Q_3^{LV}$ and $Q_4$. In this paper, we establish that the period annulus of every center in $Q_4$ has cyclicity three under quadratic perturbations, thereby proving \.{Z}o{\l}{\k{a}}dek's 1994 conjecture for this class. The proof combines Picard--Fuchs equations with a Chebyshev criterion. Its key step is a strict Wronskian inequality for two ratios of elliptic integrals on their entire interval of definition. We establish this inequality by constructing a comparison function and excluding a first zero of the Wronskian. The Chebyshev property avoids the two additional zeros allowed by the second-order differential reduction used in earlier proofs.

title: Optimal bounds for the length and number of unit fraction representations
authors: Thomas F. Bloom, Wouter van Doorn
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33241v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper gives a human-written exposition and simplification of proofs that were recently posted by OpenAI. We prove that every $a/b \in (0, 1)$ can be written as the sum of $O(\log\log b)$ many distinct unit fractions. We also prove that the number of representations of $1$ as the sum of $k$ distinct unit fractions grows doubly exponentially in $k$.

title: On the index of positivity of linear functionals: a complement to the Hermite case and new examples
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33244v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that the Dirac functional $\delta$ is the only normalized linear functional on the space of real polynomials whose index of positivity is infinite. This complements the recent study of the Hermite case by R. Sfaxi and F. Marcell\'an [Bull. Malays. Math. Sci. Soc. 48 (2025) 138]: the index of the Hermite functional $\mathcal{H}$ is finite, and so are those of $\mathcal{L}(-1/2)$, $e^{\mathcal{H}}$ and $e^{\mathcal{L}(-1/2)}$, for which the value $+\infty$ was stated there. The key observation is that real Cauchy powers act on log-moments by scaling. This yields explicit upper bounds for the index in terms of the first four moments. In particular $\mathcal{H}^n$ is not even positive for any integer $n\ge 3$, and $2\le \mathrm{Ind}_p(\mathcal{H})\le 5$. We identify the point of the original argument that needs to be modified, a free integration constant in the construction of the weights of $\mathcal{H}^n$, and we give the adjusted statements. Finally, we compute the positivity sets exactly for two new families: the real powers of $\delta_c$, which are Jacobi functionals on $[0,c]$, and the real powers of $\delta_c\delta_{-c}$, which are generalized Gegenbauer functionals containing the Chebyshev functional $\mathcal{T}$. For the latter, $\mathrm{Ind}_p(\mathcal{T})=2$. These examples show that our bounds are sharp and that every value in $[0,+\infty]$ is the index of some functional.

title: Horseshoe-Type Shrinkage from Ratio-Generated Priors
authors: Radhika Kulkarni, Anirban DasGupta, Brani Vidakovic
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33330v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a class of horseshoe-type shrinkage priors generated by ratios of independent numerator and denominator random variables. Large denominator values produce concentration near zero, small denominator values generate heavy tails, and the numerator determines scale and geometry and may also influence tail behavior. We establish general origin and tail asymptotics, including power and logarithmic singularities. Under a Gaussian likelihood and regularly varying prior tails, the posterior mean approaches the observation for large signals, with risk approaching that of the unshrunk observation.
  The denominator also induces a latent shrinkage factor. For a Cauchy denominator, this factor has exactly the ${\rm Beta}(1/2,1/2)$ distribution, whatever the numerator. With a Gaussian numerator and appropriate scale calibration, it recovers the classical horseshoe shrinkage coefficient, whereas non-Gaussian numerators can change the effective posterior shrinkage, even in its asymptotic rate.
  The Cauchy/Cauchy prior illustrates the theory, with a logarithmic singularity at the origin in one dimension, power singularities in higher dimensions, and logarithmically modified Cauchy-order tails. Its posterior mean shrinks smoothly, whereas its spatial median behaves nearly as a threshold rule. We also compare the Cauchy/Cauchy posterior mean with fifteen established shrinkage procedures on the four standard Donoho-Johnstone test functions, finding competitive, though not uniformly superior, wavelet-denoising performance.
  The ratio construction generalizes several published shrinkage priors and offers a flexible framework for sparse estimation, with natural applications to wavelet shrinkage, variable selection, and structured multivariate shrinkage.

title: Error estimates for a structure-preserving finite-element scheme of quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems
authors: Aaron Brunk, Ansgar J\"ungel, Maria Luk\'a\v{c}ov\'a-Medvid'ov\'a
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33347v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A conforming finite-element scheme for quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions is presented. The system consists of the Navier-Stokes equations, together with a quasi-incompressibility constraint, coupled with the cross-diffusion Maxwell--Stefan equations. The numerical scheme preserves the partial masses and the quasi-incompressibility constraint and dissipates the discrete energy. First-order error estimates in space and time are shown for a diffusion-augmented mobility matrix by using the relative energy method and suitable projection error estimates. Numerical experiments in two space dimensions illustrate the convergence of the scheme and indicate second-order convergence in space in the $L^2$ norm.

title: The Traveling Salesman Problem with non-convex polygonal neighborhoods: A hybrid Iterated Local Search--Block Coordinate Descent approach
authors: Ernesto G. Birgin, Paula C. R. Ertel
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33376v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem with Neighborhoods (TSPN) generalizes the classical TSP by requiring a tour to visit a set of regions in the Euclidean plane rather than fixed point coordinates. It has applications in last-mile delivery, surveillance, and remote sensing in precision agriculture. In this paper, we address the Euclidean TSPN with arbitrary, non-convex polygonal neighborhoods---a highly complex setting due to the joint continuous and combinatorial optimization challenges. To solve the continuous subproblem of determining optimal visit points for a given visiting sequence, we propose a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) method based on solving fast one-dimensional geometric subproblems. Computational experiments demonstrate that BCD computes optimal visit points for a fixed sequence in almost all instances in which optimality is certified, more than six orders of magnitude faster than a commercial solver solving the equivalent Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Programming (MIQCP) formulation. This efficiency enables an effective hybrid Iterated Local Search metaheuristic (ILS-BCD) that thoroughly explores the combinatorial search space at low computational cost. Extensive computational tests on 235 benchmark instances derived from the Generalized TSP (GTSP), with up to 100 neighborhoods, show that ILS-BCD matched or improved upon the best-known GTSP tours in all cases, obtaining strictly shorter tours in 234 instances. On the 80 instances for which optimality is proven, ILS-BCD attains the optimal tour length in all of them, within a relative difference below 0.001%. On 60 larger instances, with as many as 6,325 neighborhoods, ILS-BCD remains competitive up to about 220.

title: A Perturbative Two-Eigenvalue Faber-Krahn Problem for the Gaussian Short-Time Fourier Transform
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33401v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that, for every fixed s\in (0,\infty), the set of area s maximizing the weighted sum of the first two eigenvalues of the associated Toeplitz operators on the Fock space must be a disc, up to translations and sets of measure zero. To do so, we first prove the existence of maximizer sets. Then we show that every maximizer set must be a perturbation of a disc when the weight is sufficiently small. Finally, we use the vector-valued version of the analytic implicit function theorem and the inverse function theorem to conclude that the perturbation must vanish when the weight tends to zero.

title: A block coordinate descent method for nonconvex multiobjective optimization under H\"older continuity
authors: Lizet Santa Cruz Calder\'on, John Frank Matos Ascona, Vitaliano de Sousa Amaral, Danilo Rodrigues de Souza
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33441v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a block coordinate descent method for unconstrained multiobjective optimization problems with possibly nonconvex objectives and H\"older continuous gradients, intended for large-scale instances, in which updating all the variables simultaneously is expensive. In each iteration, only one block is updated along a descent direction common to all objectives, obtained by minimizing the maximum of their regularized quadratic models. We show that, unlike the single-objective case, stationarity on each block does not imply Pareto stationarity, and that no method that updates only the blocks of a partition of the variables and is monotone in all the objectives reaches, in general, an $\epsilon$-Pareto stationary point. Therefore, when none of the blockwise stationarity measures exceeds the tolerance, the algorithm performs a joint step across all coordinates and terminates only at $\epsilon$-Pareto stationary points. We establish a complexity bound of $O(\epsilon^{-(\beta+1)/\beta})$ iterations, where $\beta$ is the smallest H\"older exponent, the same order as that of methods that update all the variables, as well as bounds on the numbers of function and gradient evaluations, which also hold with one regularization parameter per block.

title: Using block coordinate descent for solving the close enough traveling salesman problem
authors: Ernesto G. Birgin, Paula C. R. Ertel, Rogerio S. Matos
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33448v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Close Enough Traveling Salesman Problem (CETSP) is a variant of the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem in which the salesperson must visit some point within a disk associated with each customer. Evaluating a visiting sequence requires determining an optimal visit point within each disk. This building block of virtually every CETSP algorithm is typically computed either by solving a second-order cone programming (SOCP) problem with a general-purpose solver, which can be expensive, or by discretizing the disks, which sacrifices optimality. We propose a block coordinate descent (BCD) method that computes these visit points exactly, without discretization, optimizing one visit point at a time. We show that the resulting single-disk subproblem reduces to a one-dimensional minimization, and we characterize its stationary points through the roots of a quartic polynomial. Of the three resulting solution strategies, which agree up to machine precision, Newton's method is the most efficient. Compared with an off-the-shelf SOCP solver, BCD evaluates fixed tours more than an order of magnitude faster. Embedded in an iterated local search (ILS-BCD), it finds the known optimal solutions of 720 small benchmark instances and, on 62 large ones, outperforms all heuristics of their original study in 47 and matches the best of them in 11 others. Within the memetic algorithm MA-CETSP, replacing the general-purpose SOCP solver with BCD and adding an exact local search based on the single-disk solver yields a method that, over the best of 20 runs, is better than the original algorithm in 20 of the 62 large instances and equal in the others, and improves on its best published values in 21. BCD is a fast and exact building block for evaluating visiting sequences that can replace general-purpose SOCP solvers within CETSP algorithms and enables searches that would otherwise be computationally prohibitive.

title: Quantifying combined rate- and noise-induced transitions in a multiscale system
authors: Ryan Deeley, Peter Ashwin, Ulrike Feudel
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33449v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Excitations in multiscale dynamical systems produce persistent but impermanent excursions away from a quiescent state. A novel mechanism for inducing excitations, through a combination of rate-dependent parametric and stochastic forcing, is discussed using the FitzHugh-Nagumo model as an example. In the absence of noise, a quasithreshold separating the state space between supercritical and subcritical behaviour is defined with respect to slow manifolds associated with the metastable excited state. This is formulated in an autonomous system framework, which can be obtained via a compactification of time. Techniques from singular perturbation theory elucidate how canard trajectories shape the geometric structure of the quasithreshold as the system's pullback attractor moves through it. The probability with which weakly stochastically driven sample paths travel through the quasithreshold and undertake (i) solely noise-induced and (ii) combined rate- and noise-induced excitations is estimated numerically for each of the corresponding forcing scenarios, using the adaptive multilevel splitting algorithm. The probability of weak stochastic forcing preventing a rate-induced excitation, which occurs deterministically, is likewise estimated. This quantifies the different rates at which the probability of each transition scenario scales exponentially with the noise strength, in accordance with sample path large deviation principles. It is revealed that a combination of (deterministically subcritical) parametric and stochastic forcing is exponentially more likely to induce excitations than stochastic forcing alone, which is attributed to the pullback attractor and quasithreshold converging towards one another.

title: Vector Quantized Information Bottleneck Mitigation of Adversarial Attacks on Modulation Classifiers
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33456v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) signal processing based on machine learning, including Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC), plays a critical role in Next Generation (NextG) intelligent communications but remains highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Prior work explored Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) as a means to improve robustness, but only in continuous spaces and never for RF classifiers. We investigate the impact of discrete-space information bottlenecks on the adversarial robustness of AMC models. Classification accuracy of attacked modulated RF waveforms is evaluated in two frameworks designed to leverage VIB for adversarial robustness: (i) a two-stage framework where VIB is applied in the preprocessing step using a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQVAE) to suppress adversarial perturbations in the process of input signal reconstruction and (ii) a Vector Quantized Classifier (VQC) that leverages VIB inside the classifier proper. The architectures of VQVAE and VQC are identical up to the bottleneck where the VQVAE adds a decoder while VQC utilizes a classification head. We train both VQVAE and VQC with loss functions that we derive from the VIB information-theoretic model. Both frameworks incorporate vector quantization and KL regularization to enforce discrete bottlenecks that filter out adversarial noise. Evaluations under white-box attacks demonstrate that discrete bottlenecks significantly enhance robustness: VQVAE outperforms its continuous VAE (Variational Autoencoder) counterpart, while VQC achieves strong robustness without requiring signal reconstruction.

title: Stochastic Optimization with Network Distribution Dynamics via Local Jacobian Approximation
authors: Yuchen Cai, Zhiyu He, Michael Muehlebach, Florian D\"orfler
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33466v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Network systems feature complex interactions among agents, whereby local decisions can influence the state distributions observed by other agents through coupled network dynamics. Such endogenous distribution shifts across large-scale networks pose significant challenges and call for distributed and adaptive decision-making pipelines. To address these challenges and collectively optimize a steady-state performance objective, we propose a distributed network-aware decision-response (D-NAD) gradient algorithm. This algorithm enables each agent to approximate network-response sensitivity using only local information (i.e., the Jacobians of local dynamics and objectives) and neighborhood communication. We establish a non-asymptotic closed-loop convergence guarantee and quantify the impact of the Jacobian approximation errors therein. Numerical experiments on a semi-synthetic networked electric-vehicle price--demand problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: On the non existence of minimal non-uniquely ergodic 4-IETs with flips
authors: Antonio Linero Bas, Gabriel Soler L\'opez
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33477v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The existence of minimal non uniquely ergodic oriented IETs of n intervals requires that n>= 4 by Th. 2.12 from (W. A. Veech, Interval exchange transformations, J. Anal. Math., 1978); moreover, for n=4 there exist examples of minimal non uniquely ergodic 4-IETs with two independent invariant measures, see (M. Keane, Non-ergodic interval exchange transformations, Israel J. Math., 1977). For the non oriented case, also called IETs with flips, the first examples of minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs were built in (A. Linero Bas and G. Soler L\'{o}pez, Minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs with flips, J. Differential Equations, 2023). However, the examples are (10,k)-IETs (k is the number of flips, 1<= k<= 10). Since there are no minimal (n,k)-IETs for n<= 3, it is interesting to decide if, as in the orientable case, there exist minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs with flips and four intervals. Our Main Theorem answers this question in the negative.

title: Estimation for High-Dimensional Hawkes Processes with Inhibition via CIR Approximation
authors: Nadia Belmabrouk, Mohamed Ben Alaya, Xavier Erny
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33484v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we develop a parametric estimation method for a high-dimensional Hawkes processes with inhibition. The proposed approach relies on a quantitative approximation of the Hawkes process by a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the joint large-population and long-time regime. This result requires specific techniques to handle the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient of the limiting CIR process.Based on this approximation, we construct explicit and easily implementable estimators of the model parameters. We establish their consistency and asymptotic normality. We also conduct numerical experiments to illustrate our findings.

title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33500v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.

title: The squared antipode of a twisted function algebra is locally unipotent
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33512v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $G$ be a proalgebraic group over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $F:{\rm Rep}(G)\to {\rm Vect}(k)$ be a dimension-preserving tensor functor, possibly nonsymmetric. We prove that a tensor automorphism $T$ of $F$ is locally unipotent if and only if its trace on $F(V)$ equals ${\rm dim} V$ for every $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$. Applied to the Drinfeld element of a dual twisted function algebra $(\mathcal{O}(G)^J)^*$, this proves our conjecture from 2000 that the square of the antipode in $\mathcal{O}(G)^J$ is locally unipotent (arXiv:0002128). Without the trace assumption, we show that for any $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$ the eigenvalues of $T$ on $F(V)$ determine, modulo roots of unity, its eigenvalues on $F(\mathbb{S}^\nu V)$ for every Schur functor $\mathbb{S}^\nu$. The proof combines the Koszul identity, polynomial growth of symmetric powers, Fourier inversion, and congruences for Newton sums.

title: Linear images of graphs of vector-valued affine fractal interpolation functions
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33516v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and box dimensions of every linear image of the graph of a vector-valued affine fractal interpolation function with positive vertical factors. The same formula holds for signed factors under a rank condition on the active branches. Outside an explicit finite union of hyperplanes in the space of vertical factors it holds simultaneously for all choices of interpolation knots and all linear images. The dimension is determined by the branch contractions, the rank of the projected deviations from the endpoint line, and the affine dimension of the projected knots. The proof gives uniform entropy estimates over bounded slopes for tilted projections of homogeneous triangular systems. Permutations of words with prescribed symbol frequencies then transfer the dimension estimates to unequal branch contractions. For the homogeneous systems covered by the entropy estimate, we also compute the exact dimensions of Bernoulli measures and their tilted projections. Examples with exceptional factors exhibit distinct Hausdorff and box dimensions.

title: Singular rational S-functions of second-order ODEs: structure, degree bounds and a Kovacic-type search
authors: L. G. S. Duarte, L. A. C. P. da Mota
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a rational second-order ODE $y''=phi(x,y,y')$, the $S$-function method reduces the search for a first integral to finding a rational solution $S$ of the Riccati-type equation $X(S)=S^2+phi_z S-phi_y$ along the total-derivative field $X$. The standard ansatz $S=P/N^k$, with $N=den(phi)$, misses every $S$ with poles outside $N=0$. Such singular solutions cannot be avoided: for point transforms of linear equations without hyperexponential solutions we describe every quasi-regular $S$ explicitly, and for a generic transformation none exists. We then determine the structure of singular solutions. Outside $N$ every pole is simple, with residue $-1$, and is not a Darboux surface; along non-characteristic factors of $N$ the leading polar coefficient is free Cauchy data; and the only unknown denominator is a squarefree polynomial $D$, which enters a linear equation. A Newton-polygon analysis at infinity gives the polynomial part up to a correction of bounded weight. The weighted degree of $D$ is determined exactly when the excess is zero and the top Riccati equation has no algebraic solution, and is bounded by residues of the top field otherwise, conditionally on the vanishing of that correction. The dependence of $D$ on $x$ is obtained, without a degree bound, from the rational solutions of a linear differential system. These results give a certified search procedure, implemented twice, which finds the singular $S$ of nine non-Liouvillian pull-backs of the Airy and Bessel equations. In one regime it is a decision procedure; for instance, it proves that $y''=xy+1$ has no rational $S$.

title: Adaptive Blockwise Tensor Trains for Stochastic Finite-Volume Methods with Uncertain Geometry
authors: William P. Gammel, Steven T. Walton, Stephen A. Andrews, Svetlana Tokareva, William T. Taitano
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33529v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic finite-volume (SFV) methods extend conservative, shock-capturing discretizations to hyperbolic systems with uncertain inputs by partitioning the parameter domain into finite-volume cells. However, their memory and computational cost grow exponentially with the number of uncertain parameters. Tensor-train (TT) formats can remove this exponential dependence, provided the ranks of the discrete solution remain small throughout the simulation. This requirement is frequently violated when the uncertainty is geometric. Mapping each realization onto a common reference domain introduces parameter-dependent metric factors, so that shocks and contacts propagate at different reference speeds and come to occupy different cells across realizations. The resulting rank growth is spatially localized - a structure that neither a single global TT nor a separate TT for each physical cell is able to exploit. We propose an adaptive blockwise TT representation in which the SFV solution is partitioned along its physical mode into contiguous blocks, each stored as an independent TT for every conserved variable. Blocks are split near discontinuities and in regions of large variance or rank, and merged where the solution is smooth. The mesh itself is never changed; only the grouping of cells into trains adapts. We embed this representation in a TT-based SFV solver combining WENO3 reconstruction in the physical and stochastic directions, positivity-preserving limiters, and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta time integration, with nonlinear steps evaluated via cross approximation. A mean-conservative rounding that adds no rank, together with single-valued interface fluxes, conserves the parameter-mean mass and energy to round-off for any partition. The approach is demonstrated on a Sod shock-tube problem with uncertain wall positions.

title: Stochastic Optimization for Switch-System Identification under Errors-in-Variables
authors: Yasin Garehmohammadlou, Mohamad Kazem Shirani Faradonbeh, Mohammad Khosravi, Digvijay Boob
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33545v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we address the identification of switched dynamical systems under errors-in-variables, where both input and output measurements are corrupted by noise, and the number of operating modes and subsystem orders are unknown. We propose a unified identification framework that simultaneously estimates the subsystem parameters, latent switching sequence, and model structure. The proposed formulation combines a variance-normalized data-fitting criterion with temporally regularized soft mode assignments and sparsity-inducing penalties for selecting the active modes and relevant input-output lags. To solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we develop an alternating algorithm that incorporates convex mode-assignment updates and proximal stochastic variance-reduced gradient optimization for parameter estimation. While the existing approaches in the literature require exhaustive searches over candidate structures, the proposed method performs structure selection within a single model. Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate recovery of the underlying system structure and favorable computational efficiency compared with a generalized total least squares and dynamic programming approach, particularly as the number of candidate structures increases.

title: Controllability of the Cahn Hilliard System at Finitely Many Observation Points
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33547v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study approximate controllability of the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) system with prescribed targets at finitely many points in the spatial domain. Our aim is to design a L^2 control such that given a finite set of observation points and target values, the solution reaches arbitrarily close to the prescribed targets at these points. First we study the associated linearised system using variational methods and then extend the results to the semi-linear CH system using fixed-point arguments. Further, we investigate approximate controllability in more general setting where we allow the control to be measure valued (in specific, Dirac delta type controls). This formulation is more challenging to obtain requisite regularity due to the simultaneous presence of pointwise observations and pointwise controls. Hence we restrict ourselves to the study of linearised CH system and devise a control which exhibits approximate controllability. We achieve this by approximating measure valued control with L^2 controls and showing appropriate convergence.

title: FokasNets: Completing missing boundary data in Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operators via the Global Relation
authors: Kyriakos C. Georgiou, Khemraj Shukla, Athanassios S. Fokas, George Em Karniadakis
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33549v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce FokasNets, a framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and operators (PINOs) with the Global Relation (GR) formulation of the Fokas method (also referred to as the Unified Transform), for mixed boundary problems. The general framework considers lifted representations of the neural network models, where the Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed by construction and the neural network learns the interior correction. The Global Relation is used as an additional solve during training that provides the missing boundary conditions to the lifted neural network, making training more efficient and accurate in the interior and on the boundary. We develop the construction of FokasNets for elliptic and evolution PDEs (Fokas-PINNs), and the corresponding PDE solution operator problems (Fokas Operator Networks - FONets), using the Global Relation formulations for these PDE classes. Furthermore, we develop the necessary theoretical framework for FokasNets, including error and stability analysis and show that FokasNets are universal approximators. We provide comprehensive numerical experiments, using examples with manufactured solutions and literature benchmarks. Compared to standard PINNs and Physics-Informed DeepONets and their lifted versions, FokasNets achieve significant improvements in solution accuracy in the interior and boundaries, both for single PDEs and particularly for solution operators, where the improvement reaches multiple orders of magnitude and fixed threshold errors are reached faster during training.

title: Link invariants from charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33552v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Turaev's enhanced Yang--Baxter operators produce invariants of oriented links from solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation. If the enhancing endomorphism is diagonal with generic eigenvalues, Turaev's compatibility condition forces the Yang--Baxter operator $R$ to be charge-conserving, that is, to send each $e_i\otimes e_j$ into the span of $e_i\otimes e_j$ and $e_j\otimes e_i$. Charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators were classified by Martin and Rowell. Building on their classification, we determine all enhancements of charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators with diagonal enhancing endomorphism, and we identify the resulting link invariants. The link invariant associated with such an enhancement is a sum over the colourings of the components of the link by the connected components of $R$, in which each monochromatic sublink contributes a specialization of the HOMFLY--PT polynomial and different colours interact only through linking numbers. Every such state sum arises in this way.

title: Two-timescale variational Q-learning for ergodic risk-sensitive control of Markov chains
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33554v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a variational Q-learning algorithm for the ergodic risk-sensitive control of a discrete-time Markov chain with finite state and action spaces and an unknown transition kernel. The proposed algorithm is a two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithm, where the slow iteration solves for the fixed point of the multiplicative Bellman equation cast in a variational form, while the fast iteration solves the associated optimization problem over the probability simplex that stems from the variational representation. We prove that the iterates converge almost surely to the risk-sensitive Q-function and maximizing transition kernel. The proof adapts the ODE method for two-timescale stochastic approximation, where we analyze the global asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the corresponding fast and slow ODEs as well as bound the trajectory of the fast ODE away from zero. The main challenge lies in proving that, almost surely, the slow iterates are norm-bounded and the fast iterates are bounded below away from zero on the support of the transition kernel. We address this by using a fluid scaling approach for the slow iteration combined with tailored estimates for the fast iteration to control a certain fluid-scaled relative entropy error that arises in the ODE approximation. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm and compare it with the existing risk-sensitive Q-learning algorithms.

title: The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33556v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that the classical complex Kalton--Peck space $Z_2$ is not isomorphic to $[X,H]_\theta$ for any UMD Banach space $X$, Hilbert space $H$, and $0<\theta<1$. Since $Z_2$ is UMD, this disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture on intermediate UMD spaces. The proof combines the logarithmic block identity, a shift-commutator estimate on the interpolation strip, a unified obstruction in terms of reciprocal Hilbert norms, and Hahn--Banach with elementary convexity. It allows arbitrary compatible placements. We also realize $Z_2$ as a quotient of a closed subspace of an intermediate UMD space for every fixed interpolation parameter less than one.

title: PACL: Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting framework for bound-preserving compact single-step DG methods for hyperbolic conservation laws
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33574v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting (PACL) framework for compact single-step discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of hyperbolic conservation laws. The key idea is to establish admissibility of weighted averages over overlapping cell patches after a complete high-order time step. Continuous patch weights cancel interior numerical flux contributions, yielding admissibility estimates for weighted patch averages under suitable time-step conditions. A conservative patch correction uses these averages as reference states to obtain admissible physical cell averages, and a subsequent cellwise scaling enforces whole-cell or nodal admissibility in the original DG space. The framework requires neither a strong-stability-preserving decomposition nor auxiliary first-order discretizations, and all limiting is performed at the end of each time step. For scalar conservation laws, we prove a patchwise weak maximum principle for compact Runge--Kutta DG (cRKDG), ADER-DG with converged or fixed-Picard predictors, and Lax--Wendroff DG. We also prove that, under the stated local mesh and scaling assumptions, a single application of the scalar limiter preserves approximation order at active bounds, including flat extrema. For the compressible Euler equations, we establish patch admissibility for cRKDG and fixed-Picard ADER-DG under time-step conditions that maintain positive predictor density while allowing nonpositive predictor pressure. The analysis covers both exact spatial integration and compatible quadrature. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy and bound preservation, including problems with near-vacuum states and strong shocks.

title: Solving the capacitated vehicle routing problem with polygonal neighborhoods using a metaheuristic enhanced with block coordinate descent
authors: Ernesto G. Birgin, Rog\'erio S. Matos
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33583v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) in which customers are represented by planar regions, called customer neighborhoods, rather than fixed points. Visiting a customer consists of selecting a point within its neighborhood. Therefore, besides determining the sequence of customers visited by each vehicle, one must also determine the corresponding visit points. To better reflect practical applications, customer neighborhoods are allowed to be simple polygons, either convex or non-convex, and distances are measured using the Euclidean norm. Applications include aerial reconnaissance, wireless sensor data collection and inspection, and two-stage delivery systems. We propose a general variable neighborhood search framework in which each neighbor is represented by a collection of routes. Constructing a route involves two stages, defining a customer sequence and then determining the associated visit points. The latter task is solved by a block coordinate descent (BCD) procedure, the central methodological contribution of this work, which computes high-quality visit points at a cost low enough to be used repeatedly inside the search. In extensive experiments on newly generated and adapted benchmark instances, within the time limits considered, the proposed framework matches all solutions proven optimal by CPLEX and matches or improves the best solutions found by CPLEX in the remaining instances. For the instances adapted from the CVRP literature, it also improves, in every instance, a CVRP-based upper bound given by the solution of the original CVRP instance reported in the literature, which is feasible for the problem with neighborhoods.

title: Proof of a cardinality conjecture for the correction terms in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33597v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove a conjecture due to Kato and Sagaki (arXiv:2604.04476) concerning the cardinality of sets of directed paths in the quantum Bruhat graph that occur in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom for the full flag manifolds in the quasi-minuscule case. We prove that the cadinality is equal to one or even, and its signed sum vanishes in the latter case. Consequently, the cancellation-free divisor axiom obtained by Kato and Sagaki under this conjecture holds unconditionally. The proof uses Schremmer's results on affine Bruhat order and Demazure products, together with a theorem that we prove for arbitrary Coxeter groups.

title: Sharpness of the Kadec'-type theorem for the union of intervals
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33606v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this article, we establish the sharpness of a Kadec'-type theorem for finite unions of intervals admitting the integers as an orthonormal spectrum by constructing an explicit counterexample.

title: Exact Minimum Distances of Primitive Narrow-Sense BCH Codes: At and Beyond the Bose Distance
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33613v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We determine the exact minimum distances of two families of primitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length $q^m-1$, where $q$ is a prime power and $m\geq 4$. For $1\leq i\leq\lfloor m/2\rfloor$, codes with designed distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-1$ have minimum distance and Bose distance both equal to their designed distance. Furthermore, for integers $\ell, i, s$ satisfying $3\leq\ell<\lfloor(m-1)/\ell\rfloor$, codes with designed distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-q^s-1$ have Bose distance equal to their designed distance and minimum distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-1$. Consequently, the gap between the minimum distance and the Bose distance in this family is exactly $q^s$ and grows without bound as $m$ increases, with fixed $\ell$.The proofs proceed by constructing good zero-sets from quadratic forms for the first family, and by combining upper bounds provided by the first family with lower bounds derived from the divisibility of codeword weights in punctured generalized Reed--Muller codes for the second. We also derive explicit dimension formulas by counting cyclotomic cosets.

title: Norm of the Generalized Hilbert Matrix Operator Between Some Spaces of Analytic Functions
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33616v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the generalized Hilbert operator \[ \mathcal H_bf(z)=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^b}{(1-tz)^{b+1}}f(t)\,dt, \qquad b>0, \] on several spaces of analytic functions in the unit disk. For logarithmically weighted Korenblum spaces, we obtain an exact supremum representation and a lower estimate for the norm of the mapping from $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$ to $H_\alpha^\infty$. We then establish two-sided estimates and characterize the boundedness range of $\mathcal H_b$ on the $\alpha$-Bloch spaces $\mathcal B^\alpha$. We also derive norm bounds for the mapping from $H^\infty$ into the endpoint Zygmund-type space $\Lambda_1^{1,*}$. Furthermore, we give a norm representation for $\mathcal H_b:H_\alpha^\infty\to\mathcal B^{\alpha+1}$ and identify a norm-attaining function. In particular, for $0<\alpha\leq2/3$, the norm is expressed explicitly in terms of a Beta function. Finally, we obtain an exact supremum representation of the norm of $\mathcal H_b$ on $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$, together with explicit norm estimates. Our results extend those of Hao et al. [J. Geom. Anal. 35 (2025), Paper No. 184] for the classical Hilbert matrix operator ($b=0$) to the generalized case $b>0$.

title: Anderson-Accelerated Landweber Iteration with Regularization Guarantees for Nonlinear Ill-Posed Problems
authors: Jianming Gao, Xiliang Lu, Lin Tian
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33677v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Anderson acceleration (AA) can markedly reduce iteration counts for fixed-point solvers, but its unrestricted signed history extrapolation need not preserve the stability required for iterative regularization of ill-posed problems. We introduce a regularization-guaranteed Anderson-accelerated Landweber method (\RG) in which finite-memory AA generates a proposal while the committed iterate is a controlled perturbation of a certified Landweber anchor. Under a local tangential cone condition and a scale-normalized localization condition, we prove strong convergence of the exact-data trajectory to a solution, stability at every fixed iteration, finite discrepancy stopping, and strong convergence of the discrepancy-stopped noisy reconstructions to the same exact-data limit; local uniqueness is needed only if that selected limit is to be identified with a prescribed solution $x^\dagger$. Under the additional benchmark source condition $x^\dagger-x_0=F'(x^\dagger)^*\lambda^\dagger$ and a standard range-invariance condition, we obtain the discrepancy-principle rate $\norm{x_{k_\delta}^\delta-x^\dagger}=O(\delta^{1/2})$. The rate proof controls data-dependent Anderson coefficients through fixed memory, a fixed-reference ridge in the small AA least-squares problem, and an outer correction budget with an $O(k^{-1})$ tail. The numerical examples verify the efficiency of the proposed method.

title: A Stackelberg strategy for the semi-linear heat equation with boundary controls
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33683v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This work continues the results presented in \cite{calsavara2022new} where a hierarchical control problem is solved. Our first goal is the case of both controls acting on the boundary. The follower control solves a null controllability problem, and the leader minimizes a $L^2$ cost functional. Additionally, we solve the case where one control acts on the boundary and the other on an open subset of the domain. More precisely, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a leader-follower couple and give some techniques to solve the problem.

title: A fast tangential rational Krylov subspace method with randomized sketching for large Lyapunov matrix equations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33684v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a tangential rational Krylov subspace method augmented with randomized sketching for solving continuous-time Lyapunov equations $AX + XA^T + BB^T = 0$, where $A$ is large and sparse and $B$ has a rank much higher than one. Numerical solutions require high-dimensional rational Krylov subspaces (e.g., of dimensions up to $\sim 1000$), leading to substantial computational cost and long runtime. Building on the adaptive strategies of [SIAM\,J.\,Matrix\,Anal.\,Appl., 35\,(2014), pp.\,476--498], which expand the subspace using the most relevant directions, we introduce several enhancements: selective orthogonalization of basis vectors and fast residual-norm estimation enabled by randomized sketching, and the option to use either adaptive distinct poles or a small set of repeated poles. We derive a new computable error bound for the approximate solutions and show that sketching does not degrade the convergence rate relative to the standard (non-sketched) algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved robustness and efficiency, with reduced runtimes and often higher accuracy than the standard tangential method.

title: Two 3-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problems for Wave-like Equations With a Single Location of the Point Source
authors: Michael V. Klibanov, Jingzhi Li, Tian Niu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33688v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper two long standing open questions are addressed for the first time. Those questions are about Lipschitz stability estimates and uniqueness theorems for two Coefficient Inverse Problems (CIPs) for 3-Dimensional wave-like Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with formally determined input data. We assume that a certain associated PDE is written in finite differences with respect to time t. The unknown coefficients depend on all three spatial variables. The key novelty here is that the input data for these CIPs are generated by only a single location of the point source at the moment of time {t = 0}. In the first CIP (CIP1) the unknown coefficient is the potential of a wave-like PDE. The second CIP (CIP2) is concerned with a far more challenging case when the unknown coefficient is involved in the principal part of the hyperbolic operator. In addition to Lipschitz stability and uniqueness results, numerical methods are developed for both CIPs. Their convergence analysis establishes the global convergence property of both numerical techniques. The latter is unlike the local convergence of conventional numerical procedures for CIPs. The method for CIP1 is tested computationally. Its extensive numerical testing for complicated media structures consistently demonstrates a very accurate performance of this method for noisy input data. The authors declare that artificial intelligence was not used for any part of this work.

title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33753v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ternary binding systems occur in signaling, scaffold-mediated assembly, and targeted protein degradation. A mediator brings two partners into a productive ternary complex, but excess mediator can hold them in separate binary complexes. Consequently, ternary complex formation can increase and then decrease as the mediator dose increases, producing the hook effect. Deterministic dose-response curves describe the average behavior but do not indicate whether individual small compartments reliably form the complex. A minimal reversible binding network was studied using deterministic equations, exact stochastic simulations, and a simple catalytic extension. The deterministic model recovered the hook-shaped response. In stochastic simulations, small volumes often failed to accumulate the required number of complexes, even where the deterministic prediction was favorable. At low mediator doses, failure reflected a shortage of mediator molecules; at high doses, material accumulated in free or binary-bound forms. Larger volumes increased the range of mediator doses supporting reliable formation, while stricter copy-number thresholds narrowed that range. Faster ternary-complex completion or slower breakup improved reliability. In the catalytic model, product formation also depended on how early productive complexes formed. These results show why a favorable average binding response does not necessarily ensure reliable assembly in small reaction volumes.

title: A Nonlocal Allen--Cahn Model for Volume-Constrained Wetting and Its Multi-Structure-Preserving Discretization
authors: Yadong Liu, Nan Lu, Zhonghua Qiao, Yuze Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33754v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: At finite interface thickness, small droplets can shrink or disappear during wetting relaxation even when the phase-field mass is conserved. We develop a nonlocal Allen--Cahn model that couples a nonlinear diffuse-volume constraint to dynamic wall relaxation through Onsager's principle. The constraint gradient vanishes at the pure-phase values and does zero work in the energy balance, preserving the original bulk and wall dissipation structure. We construct a Compatible Variational Chain-Rule (CVC) scheme using the same discrete derivative of the volume density in the correction and in the volume increment. The scheme exactly conserves the nonlinear diffuse volume and reproduces the bulk--wall dissipation identity for the original discrete energy. Under a coercivity condition, the energy also yields a mesh-dependent maximum-norm bound. Numerical tests show second-order convergence in space and time. In flat-wall tests, the proposed model improves small-droplet retention and geometric-volume preservation and reproduces equilibrium cap shapes and contact angles. Additional tests illustrate wetting on chemically heterogeneous and rough substrates.

title: Universal Stabilization with Six Records
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33762v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This letter shows that a single feedback controller needs only six retained observation records to handle the largest universally stabilizable uncertainty range for the scalar discrete-time benchmark model of Xie and Guo, when uncertainty is measured by the radius of a generalized Lipschitz ball. Existing constructions can require arbitrarily many records along bounded trajectories. Our controller retains at most six genuine state-response pairs and five auxiliary real scalars. Each update requires a uniformly bounded number of elementary operations. No knowledge of the plant, its generalized Lipschitz constants, or the disturbance bound is required.

title: A Non-Commutative Binomial Theorem, Extensions, and Applications
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33774v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents a matrix trace inequality analogous to the binomial theorem for reals: for Hermitian matrices $A$ and $B$, and a nonnegative even integer $k$ (and any nonnegative integer $k$ when $A, B$ are positive semi-definite), \[ \mathrm{tr}\bigl((A + B)^k\bigr) \le \sum_{\ell=0}^k \binom{k}{\ell} \mathrm{tr}\bigl(A^\ell B^{k-\ell}\bigr). \] The above natural inequality implies the classical Golden--Thompson inequality $\mathrm{tr}(e^{A + B}) \le \mathrm{tr}(e^A e^B)$. It also proves an extension, which can be used to show other new inequalities as well as give short proofs of inequalities such as the Schatten-$p$ two-point inequality for $p \ge 3$ and Hanner's inequality for $p \ge 3$.
  The main proof was discovered by Gemini Carbon within an agentic system.

title: Sections and Constant Fields of Postcritically Finite Rational Maps
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33780v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We relate the constant fields of generic preimage towers to two invariants of geometric monodromy. Bounded section indices characterize branching of the closed action and imply a finite constant extension. Unbounded finite-level abelianization orders force an infinite cyclotomic subextension. For a quadratic rational map with hyperbolic orbifold, we compute the section indices and abelianizations at every sufficiently large level and obtain an infinite real cyclotomic subextension. We also give a branching criterion for quadratic maps with neither critical point periodic and formulate three conjectures about the discrete action, the constants, and the case of bounded abelianizations with unbounded section indices.

title: Variance Reduction Note 6: The Convergence of SAGA
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: SAGA corrects a sampled component gradient with a table of previously computed gradients. Updating one entry at a time gives an unbiased gradient estimate at the cost of one new component gradient per iteration. This sixth note on variance reduction proves a linear convergence guarantee for a smooth finite sum with convex components and a strongly convex average. A two-component quadratic shows how the spread of the stored evaluation points determines the variance, even at the minimizer. We track the iterate and the table jointly to obtain a last-iterate bound, then relate its dependence on the sample size to the rate at which individual entries are replaced. For generalized linear losses the same gradient table can be represented by one scalar per observation and a running mean.

title: BGPNP: A Non-Euclidean Gradient Projection Newton Pursuit Method for Sparsity-Constrained Optimization
authors: Jiawei Chen, Huilin Han, Yibing Lv, Jen-Chih Yao
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33802v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A non-Euclidean gradient projection Newton pursuit method is proposed for solving sparsity constrained optimization problem via the Bregman distance. The method is also denoted as BGPNP. The method firstly constructs a gradient projection step based on the Bregman distance to ensure that the iterates satisfy the sparsity constraint. Then, when the support set becomes stable or the gradient norm is sufficiently small, a Newton pursuit step is introduced to improve local convergence efficiency. The BGPNP is proved to possess a sufficient descent property and the non-increasing monotonicity of the objective function values. The full convergence and linear convergence rate of the BGPNP are established under appropriate conditions, which do not involve the symmetry coefficient of Bregman distance and the $\theta$-uniform condition. Moreover, the locally quadratical convergence rate of the BGPNP is also obtained. This method provides an effective algorithmic framework for sparse optimization in non-Euclidean setting. Numerical experiments on sparsity-constrained compressed sensing problems validate the competitive performance of BGPNP compared with existing leading solvers.
